title: Crossplane-bridge and primitive module refactor roadmap
content:
Purpose

This doc captures a pragmatic roadmap for refactoring our Terraform primitive modules (VPC, IAM, cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS) to: (1) simplify variable surface area, (2) stabilize outputs as a contract, (3) enable a Crossplane bridge for customers who want Kubernetes-native provisioning in private deployments, and (4) provide a safe upgrade path with canaries and automated validation.

Audience
- Infra engineers owning private-deploy primitives
- Solutions engineers onboarding on-prem customers
- Release/sre for rollout and rollback playbooks

Non-goals
- Rewriting provider implementations (we keep using official cloud providers).
- Full Crossplane operator implementation here — we propose a bridge pattern.

Assumptions
- Existing modules are widely used across private-deploy and some Dedicated setups.
- Backwards compatibility is critical for output names used by downstream TF modules and customer stacks.
- We can introduce a compatibility shim layer for 6 months before sunsetting legacy outputs.

High-level approach
1) Introduce a thin ‘compat’ outputs facade in each primitive module that maps new stable outputs -> legacy names. This facade is separately toggleable via a boolean variable (legacy_output_compat = true).
2) Consolidate variables into three layers: metadata (tags/labels), topology (cidr, subnets, azs), and policy (IAM flags, encryption keys). Provide a single map variable 'primitive_config' as the recommended entrypoint for new users to reduce combinatorial args.
3) Implement Crossplane bridge as a separate module (tf-crossplane-bridge) that:
   - Re-uses the module outputs to create Crossplane Composition resources (via templated YAML in a k8s_manifest resource) when customers request k8s-native interface.
   - Does not change TF module core behavior — bridge only reads outputs.
4) Upgrade plan: phased canary across internal clusters, partner pilot, broad rollout, and deprecation window for legacy outputs.

Module interface proposals
- vpc-primitive module (existing name: vpc-primitive)
  - New recommended vars: primitive_config (map), environment (string), legacy_output_compat (bool, default true)
  - Deprecated vars: lots of long booleans/flags to be surfaced under primitive_config
  - Stable outputs (new): vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, routing_table_ids, nat_gateway_ids, cidr_block
  - Legacy outputs (old): vpc_id_old, public_subnets, private_subnets, route_tables, nat_ids, network_cidr
  - Behavior: when legacy_output_compat=true, module continues to expose both sets. When false, only stable outputs are exposed.

- iam-primitive module
  - New stable outputs: role_arn_admin, role_arn_node, policy_attachment_ids
  - Variables: primitive_config. For existing boolean features (enable_s3_access), map under primitive_config["features"]["s3"] = true

- cluster-primitive module (EKS/GKE/AKS)
  - Single module interface with provider switch: provider = "aws"|"gcp"|"azure" to pick cluster type. Internals use submodules per cloud but keep a shared variable/output contract.
  - Stable outputs: cluster_name, kubeconfig, node_security_group_id, autoscaling_group_ids (if applicable), control_plane_endpoint
  - Outputs should be cloud-agnostic names (e.g., kubeconfig_blob rather than aws_eks_kubeconfig).

Compatibility and output facade
- Add outputs.tf that defines new stable outputs and then conditional legacy aliases:
  output "vpc_id" { value = aws_vpc.main.id }
  output "vpc_id_old" { value = aws_vpc.main.id if var.legacy_output_compat else null }
- Provide a migration helper script (scripts/migrate-outputs.sh) to scan downstream modules and produce a mapping report for deprecations. This will be run in CI for every PR that touches outputs.

Crossplane bridge design notes
- Rationale: Many customers (especially enterprise private customers) prefer to manage infra via k8s CRs. Crossplane provides composition patterns; we want to offer a supported bridge instead of forcing a full rewrite.
- Implementation: a tf module (tf-crossplane-bridge) that takes primitive module outputs and renders a Crossplane Composition YAML for: VPC, Subnets, Cluster, IAM Roles. It will use "local_file" or k8s provider to apply manifests into a management cluster.
- Safety: Bridge is opt-in at customer onboarding. It runs after TF apply, and includes idempotency checks (hashes of last-applied manifest) so it doesn't overwrite manual edits without explicit reconcile flag.

Upgrade & rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (preparation, 2 weeks): clean up tests, add outputs facade, add legacy_output_compat flag, update examples. Create test fixtures for each cloud.
- Phase 1 (internal canary, 2 weeks): pick 3 internal non-customer clusters (aws/gcp/azure) and run upgrade flow with legacy_output_compat=true then flip to false for one cluster to validate downstream compatibility.
- Phase 2 (partner pilot, 4 weeks): opt-in pilot with 2 customers (one on-prem, one VPC in cloud) using Crossplane bridge. Collect regressions and migration pain points.
- Phase 3 (broad rollout, 6 weeks): flip default legacy_output_compat to false in new major module release but keep a module var that can be set. Notify customers 30d in advance via notices and migration guide.
- Phase 4 (deprecation window, 180 days): after 180 days and migration assistance, remove legacy aliased outputs in the following major version.

Testing and CI
- Add a test matrix in CI that runs: plan/apply/destroy for each primitive on small test accounts (staging projects). Use terratest or kitchen-terraform for E2E probes.
- Add unit tests for output names (conftest/OPA) that fail PRs introducing new outputs without aliasing or migration notes.
- Add a smoke-check post-upgrade: run downstream modules that reference legacy outputs and assert they get the same values via new outputs using a mapping script.

Migration checklist (for infra owner updating stacks)
- Run scripts/migrate-outputs.sh to get mapping report.
- Replace references to legacy outputs in downstream modules: e.g., replace module.vpc.network_cidr -> module.vpc.cidr_block
- Run terraform plan in a drift-safe environment (staging) and validate there are no destructive changes.
- Flip legacy_output_compat=false and re-run plan to ensure nothing breaks.
- For customers using variable-by-variable patterns (not primitive_config), convert to primitive_config progressively. We provide shim variables for 6 months.

On-prem caveats
- KMS/HSM integrations: outputs should include keys or key aliases, but access patterns differ on-prem. Provide a provider-neutral output: encryption_key_ref. Document mapping to customer KMS/HSM.
- Network topology: on-prem often cannot create AZ-separated subnets; cluster-primitive must support single-AZ topology via variable primitive_config["topology"]["az_aware"] = false.
- Connectivity: when private deployments use existing transit networks, module should accept external routing_table_ids via primitive_config to avoid creating overlapping resources.

Rollback and emergency controls
- For each release, provide a v1-to-v0 rollback patch that re-introduces legacy outputs unconditionally (temporary).
- Build a safety script (scripts/check-legacy-references.rb) that enumerates all terraform state references to legacy outputs across org repos to measure exposure before rollout.

Implementation timeline (rough)
- Week 0-2: design review, tests scaffold, output facade implementation (all primitives)
- Week 3-5: crossplane-bridge prototype + internal demos
- Week 6-8: internal canary upgrades + partner sign-ups
- Week 9-16: pilot feedback, iterate, broad release prep

Open questions / risks
- How to handle downstream modules maintained by third parties (public examples)? We can provide a compatibility adapter repo and installable shim module.
- Edge-case outputs that embed cloud-specific resource ARNs — should we provide both stable cloud-agnostic and raw cloud-specific outputs? Proposal: both, but raw ones are flagged as cloud_specific_*.
- Crossplane maintenance burden — we need to decide if we will support the bridge long-term or hand off to a partner.

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Aisha: create PR skeleton for output facade (ETA 2024-09-25)
- Diego: prototype tf-crossplane-bridge (ETA 2024-10-09)
- Lena: add CI tests and OPA policies for outputs (ETA 2024-10-02)
- Omar: run org-wide legacy reference scan and produce report (JIRA-OPS-1297) (ETA 2024-09-27)

Appendix: example variable mapping (recommended new primitive_config)
primitive_config = {
  "metadata" = { "name_suffix" = "-dev", "tags" = { "team" = "ml-platform" } }
  "topology" = { "cidr_block" = "10.20.0.0/16", "public_subnet_sizes" = ["/24","/24"], "az_aware" = true }
  "policy" = { "enable_nat" = true, "encryption_key_ref" = "projects/xyz/keys/kms1" }
}

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep examples lean and add code snippets to the examples/ directory not in root of module.
- Notify support and solutions-engineering BEFORE flipping defaults.
- Collect customer beta volunteers by Oct 7.

References
- internal: confluence:privdeploy/module-stability-notes
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra (see linked PR)
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1297 (legacy output scan)
